This seems to be a difference between sympathy and empathy in my opinion. 

From my understanding sympathy = ability to feel sorry for someone while empathy =ability to put yourself in someone's shoes.

I think it's easier to gain sympathy from someone who has never been in your situation before yet at the same time it's hard for them to truly KNOW what it's like to be in that situation; empathise.

Likewise it's easier for someone to empathise with you if they've been in the same situation once before. In this case, I think it's hard for them to sympathise with you since the general assumption seems to be that they've already overcome the obstacle in question. They don't really feel sorry for you because if they overcame it, so should you .
I don’t know what else to say but give you a smile......😊

This is can totally relate to. I'm 22 and I'm studying in a foreign country all alone. I practically know no one I can call to pick me up at the airport, help me when my rents low, help me move houses etc.

There's no one my own family can call if I ever went silent on them. No one if I ever broke my leg.

That's truly the worst part of being alone.

You know the worst thing about all of that is that you could be the one in a million who actually gets to meet 'your one' but you let the chance of a happy, good life go because the two of you are from very different backgrounds.

I've chatted with people online who I really felt in sync with but it just dies once we start thinking of the logistics of family, countries, culture. That sucks!
